rationale: A wins because it keeps the causal claim on a leash: “The story isn't the robot; it's the pairing” is a real restaurant-operations angle without pretending Chipotle proved the math. B has usable bones, but “Its Avocado Robot Explains Why” and “Competitors Are Taking Notes” sell inference as fact. That is how a decent pitch gets turned into a correction email.
gaps_in_A: “the first evidence that a major chain is automating a full assembly-line format” overreaches. The update supports two robot systems, not first evidence or full-line automation.
“the two statements were made together” is treated as established. The supplied update pairs the facts, but does not explicitly say Chipotle announced them together.
“The margin question survives longer” is plausible, but still needs outside market context before it becomes more than company-news analysis.
gaps_in_B: “Its Avocado Robot Explains Why” states causality the update does not prove. The set later admits the link is only implied, but the headline already spent the credibility.
“Labor Advocates Are Watching” invents a reaction. The update says no job cuts; it does not say advocates, unions, or researchers are currently watching.
“Its Competitors Are Taking Notes” is unsupported. No competitor response, analyst note, or category signal was supplied.
“Chipotle Says Its Robots Justify Flat Prices” is not grounded. Chipotle says prices stay flat and robots are rolling out; it did not say robots justify the price decision.
